articles.title: Papa León XIV reaparece en el Ángelus y dice que retomará gradualmente su actividad
articles.summary: Tras reaparecer en el rezo del ángelus en el Vaticano, el papa León XIV agradeció las muestras de apoyo recibidas durante su convalecencia por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, del que fue operado el pasado martes en Roma
articles.body_text: Tras su alta hospitalaria, el papa León XIV reapareció este domingo en el rezo del Ángelus en el Vaticano, donde explicó que, una vez superada la etapa de su operación pulmonar por un tumor canceroso, retomará sus actividades gradualmente. “Una vez superada esta difícil etapa, como saben, retomaré gradualmente mis actividades, siempre con la ayuda de Dios y sus oraciones”, dijo el pontífice, de 71 años, tras el rezo del Ángelus ante los miles de fieles que se congregaron en la plaza de San Pedro. A las doce del mediodía, León XIV apareció en la ventana de sus aposentos en el Palacio Apostólico vaticano, con buen aspecto, sonriente y saludando a los fieles, que le dedicaron una sonora ovación desde la plaza: “Queridos hermanos y hermanas, ¡buen domingo!, fueron sus primeras palabras antes de comenzar con la plegaria del ángelus. Tras el rezo, el pontífice compartió unas reflexiones, en una alocución más breve de lo que suele ser habitual en estos actos y que aprovechó para dar las gracias a todos los que han orado por él en estos días: “He sentido profundamente su apoyo. ¡Muchas gracias!”. También dedicó su especial gratitud a los médicos, enfermeras y todo el personal del Políclinico Gemelli, donde el pasado martes fue operado de un adenocarcinoma en su pulmón derecho y donde ha estado ingresado hasta ayer sábado, recuperándose de la cirugía. “Esta experiencia me ha acercado especialmente a quienes sufren enfermedades y dolencias”, manifestó Robert Prevost, cuya reaparición en el ángelus duró unos ocho minutos, incluyendo plegaria y alocución posterior. En la plaza de San Pedro, los fieles vivieron con emoción y alegría la reaparición del papa este domingo, según testimonios recabados por EFE: “Pensábamos que no lo íbamos a ver, estamos contentas porque la divina providencia lo permitió”, manifestaron Cindy y Emilia, dos colombianas que expresaron su deseo de que el papa mejore “y lo tengamos muchos años más”. “Tenemos fe en que va a salir todo bien”, decían convencidas Patricia y Rose Esperanza, procedentes de California (EE.UU), para quienes ver hoy a León XIV ha sido “un sueño”. También Ernesto Villegas, sacerdote venezolano, reconocía que el de este domingo ha sido un ángelus de mucha expectación y elogió la fortaleza del pontífice: “El papa ha demostrado es un hombre de armas tomar, no se acobarda, retoma su agenda y sigue adelante como buen pastor que sigue dando la vida por sus ovejas”, dijo a EFE. Hace justo una semana que León XIV, en este mismo rezo, anunció por sorpresa a todo el mundo una inminente operación por la detección de un nódulo en un pulmón. La operación se produjo dos días después, el martes por la tarde, en el hospital Gemelli de Roma: el parte médico posterior informó de la extirpación del lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho del papa por un adenocarcinoma, un tipo de cáncer. En los días posteriores, León XIV ha tenido una recuperación favorable y, en el momento de su alta, presentaba unas condiciones clínicas “absolutamente satisfactorias”, según Stefano Margaritora, el cirujano que le operó y que dirige la unidad de Cirugía Torácica del Gemelli. La reaparición del papa en el ángelus desde el Vaticano ha despertado expectación también por la posibilidad de que ofreciera detalles sobre su tratamiento o sobre el viaje a Argentina, Uruguay y Perú que está programado del 6 al 17 de noviembre, si bien Robert Prevost no ha hecho referencia a estos temas. Ayer sábado, en una entrevista a medios vaticanos, su cirujano afirmó que el papa puede afrontar esa visita apostólica: “Diría que no hay motivos clínicos por los que no se pueda realizar ese viaje”, manifestó el doctor Margaritora. En esta primera gira latinoamericana del pontificado de León XIV están previstos hasta 14 vuelos, más de cuarenta discursos y reuniones, nueve misas multitudinarias, así como la visita a Cusco, una ciudad situada a más de 3.000 metros sobre el nivel del mar. articles.title: Conadis lanza grave advertencia: gobiernos regionales y municipios desvían recursos destinados para atender a personas con discapacidad
articles.summary: Presidenta del Conadis, Olga Villalobos, indicó que los gobiernos locales y regionales “le están sacando la vuelta” a la ley, ya que destina el presupuesto para atender a personas con discapacidad a otras áreas o implementan oficinas sin brindar ningún servicio
articles.body_text: El 16 de octubre se conmemora en el país el Día Nacional de la Persona con Discapacidad, por lo que El Comercio entrevistó a Olga Mercedes Villalobos, presidenta del Consejo Nacional para la Integración de la Persona con Discapacidad (Conadis), para conocer los objetivos de su gestión y los retos que afronta un ciudadano con discapacidad en el país. Un punto saltante de la entrevista es que, según Villalobos, los gobiernos regionales y las municipalidades reportan que destinan recursos para supuestamente atender a las personas con discapacidad, pero remarcó que se ha comprobado que existen oficinas que no ofrecen ningún tipo de servicio o el presupuesto se destina a otras áreas. 1. ¿Cuál es el rol de Conadis frente a una persona con discapacidad? El rol del Conadis es promover y garantizar el reconocimiento y ejercicio de los derechos de las personas con discapacidad, impulsando políticas públicas, articulando acciones con las entidades del Estado en sus tres niveles de gobierno y supervisando el cumplimiento de las obligaciones fiscalizables. Asimismo, brinda orientación a las personas con discapacidad y sus familias, promueve la eliminación de barreras que limitan su participación en la sociedad y contribuye a generar las condiciones necesarias para que puedan ejercer sus derechos en igualdad de condiciones con las demás personas. 2. ¿Cuáles son los objetivos de su gestión? Soy una educadora especialista en discapacidad y lo más importante en este momento es el tema de la educación inclusiva, ya que, sin ella, una persona con discapacidad no podrá tener oportunidades a nivel de estudios técnicos productivos y a nivel universitario, por tanto, seguirá estando en un círculo de pobreza. 3. ¿Qué retos afronta una persona con discapacidad en el Perú? En el Perú, las personas con discapacidad enfrentan múltiples barreras que dificultan el ejercicio pleno de sus derechos y su participación en igualdad de condiciones en la sociedad. Entre los principales retos se encuentran persistencia de prejuicios, estereotipos y prácticas discriminatorias, así como barreras de accesibilidad en los espacios públicos, el transporte público, la información y las comunicaciones. También enfrenta dificultades para acceder a una educación inclusiva, servicios de salud de calidad y oportunidades de empleo digno. A ello se suman las brechas territoriales, especialmente en las zonas rurales, la limitada disponibilidad de servicios de apoyo y las dificultades para ejercer su autonomía. Desde el 2012 no se hace una Enedis (Encuesta Nacional Especializada sobre Discapacidad) y hemos pedidos de manera reiterada al MEF que nos asigne el presupuesto de 16 millones de soles para realizar esta encuesta especializada a través del INEI. Si no se conoce la brecha, es muy difícil generar políticas públicas. Necesitamos saber dónde está la persona con discapacidad, qué discapacidad tiene y cuál es su necesidad. 4. ¿Cómo ha venido evolucionando el tema de los derechos para las personas con discapacidad en las últimas décadas? Nuestra legislación ha experimentado importantes cambios en la manera de comprender la discapacidad, transitando del modelo médico-rehabilitador al modelo social y de derechos humanos, que reconoce la importancia de eliminar las barreras del entorno. 5. ¿A cuántas personas con discapacidad el Conadis brinda asistencia o cuántas personas tiene registradas? A través del Registro Nacional de la Persona con Discapacidad, el Conadis cuenta, al 15 de octubre de 2026, con 631 330 inscripciones. Asimismo, mediante la Red Alivia Perú, uno de nuestros principales servicios de orientación y acompañamiento, hemos atendido a 26,720 personas en lo que va del año, facilitándoles el acceso a información, servicios públicos y el ejercicio de derechos de las personas con discapacidad y sus familias. 6. ¿Conadis realiza visitas inopinadas para garantizar servicios de calidad a personas con discapacidad? Conadis ejerce su competencia de fiscalización y sanción a través de la Dirección de Fiscalización y Sanciones. Anualmente aprueba un Plan de Fiscalizaciones y estas se desarrollan de acuerdo con un programa establecido. Durante el año 2026, se realizaron 527 fiscalización a nivel nacional. De este total, 313 corresponden a fiscalizaciones ordinarias, cuyo objetivo es verificar el cumplimiento de la normativa y, de detectarse incumplimientos, pueden dar lugar al inicio de un procedimiento administrativo sancionador; y 214 corresponden a fiscalizaciones orientativas, de carácter preventivo. A diferencia de las ordinarias, estas acciones no tienen como finalidad imponer sanciones, sino brindar recomendaciones y asistencia técnica para que las entidades adecuen su actuación a la normativa vigente. Asimismo, estamos efectuando supervisiones a las Omaped para verificar su implementación y prestación de servicios a las personas con discapacidad. Se han visitado más de 40 Omaped en Lima. 7. ¿Qué expectativas tiene respecto al anuncio de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori de que el próximo año se ampliará el presupuesto del programa social Contigo a fin de incorporar a más de 100,000 personas con discapacidad? En realidad, es un hecho histórico que ha logrado la gestión de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori en articulación con la ministra de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables, Mara Seminario. Desde el año 2024 solo eran beneficiarios 142,771 y la proyección del presupuesto para el 2027 no estaba contemplado un aumento, situación que como Conadis nos preocupaba porque había en lista de espera un promedio de 116,200 personas. En las anteriores gestiones de gobierno no se tuvo la prioridad de ampliar la atención de la pensión, que es de 300 soles bimensuales a las personas con discapacidad. Los requisitos para acceder a la pensión son: ser una persona con discapacidad severa y estar en situación de pobreza. 8. ¿Se cumple la norma que establece que las entidades públicas deben contratar un mínimo de 5% de su personal con personas con discapacidad, mientras que, en el sector privado, las empresas con más de 50 trabajadores deben destinar al menos el 3%? Los resultados obtenidos en las fiscalizaciones realizadas por el Conadis evidencian que solo un ministerio, específicamente el Ministerio de Trabajo y Promoción del Empleo, cumple con la cuota laboral del 5% para las personas con discapacidad. Asimismo, a nivel de gobierno regionales, en las fiscalizaciones realizadas en el año 2025 solo 4 GORE cumplen la cuota: Pasco, Piura, Huánuco y Ucayali. En lo va del 2026, Conadis realizó 82 fiscalizaciones en materia de cumplimiento de la cuota de empleo, y se verificó que 14 entidades cumplieron con la cuota legal del 5%, mientras que 62 entidades no cumplieron con dicha obligación. En los 6 casos restantes, no fue posible determinar el cumplimiento debido a que las entidades administradas no remitieron la información completa requerida para efectuar la evaluación correspondiente. Por otro lado, debemos precisar que, de conformidad con la normativa actual, corresponde al Ministerio de Trabajo, a través de Sunafil, la fiscalización en el ámbito privado. De acuerdo con la información de Sunafil, 245 empresas privadas cumplen con la cuota de empleo para personas con discapacidad en el 2025. 9. ¿Se ha avanzado en el cumplimiento de la norma que dispone que los gobiernos regionales y locales deben destinar el 1% de su presupuesto anual a favor de la población con discapacidad? Mediante la Ley Nº 32139 se estableció que los gobiernos regionales y locales tienen la obligación de contemplar en su presupuesto anual recursos para actividades, que es el 0.5% del Presupuesto Institucional de Apertura para Oredis y Omaped, así como el 0.5% del PIA en inversiones para proyectos y mantenimiento de accesibilidad. El Conadis ha encontrado que, de 24 gobiernos regionales fiscalizados/supervisados, ninguno ha cumplido con asignar el 0.5% de los recursos para financiar actividades y proyectos orientados a la atención de las personas con discapacidad. Asimismo, de 60 gobiernos locales fiscalizados osupervisados, sólo han asignado más del 0.5% de recursos para actividades unos 26 gobiernos locales; mientras que 5 han destinado más del 0.5% para proyectos. El ente rector de fiscalización es la Contraloría. La norma era una esperanza para las personas con discapacidad, ya que se tiene un presupuesto destinado, lo cual en algunos gobiernos regionales es bastante dinero, ya que en determinados casos hay más de 20 millones de soles para destinarlo a la Oficinas Regionales de Atención a las Personas con Discapacidad (Oredis) o a la Oficina Municipal de Atención a la Persona con Discapacidad (Omaped). Sin embargo, ningún GORE ha dado el 1% para temas de discapacidad. Por eso, la persona con discapacidad está tan disconforme y abandonada, ya que hay un presupuesto, pero no se le asigna. Unos cinco gobiernos regionales han cerrado sus Oredis para que ese presupuesto ya no entre a esa oficina y se destine a la Gerencia de Desarrollo Social a fin de distribuirlo a sus diferentes programas sociales. Le han sacado la vuelta a la ley. Hemos quedado con el titular de la PCM, Luis Galarreta, y la ministra de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables, Mara Seminario, que ni bien se dé las credenciales a las nuevas autoridades municipales y regionales se realizará una inducción sobre la ley que obliga a destinar el 1% para temas de accesibilidad y servicios, ya que tiene una sanción penal. En el caso de Omaped, se ha detectado que en la consulta amigable del MEF se consigna que sí han asignado el 0.5% del presupuesto, sin embargo, cuando se visita el local de Omaped no hay ningún servicio, lo que lleva a preguntarse a dónde se está yendo el dinero.

articles.title: Papa León XIV reaparece en el Ángelus y dice que retomará gradualmente su actividad
articles.summary: Tras reaparecer en el rezo del ángelus en el Vaticano, el papa León XIV agradeció las muestras de apoyo recibidas durante su convalecencia por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, del que fue operado el pasado martes en Roma
articles.body_text: Tras su alta hospitalaria, el papa León XIV reapareció este domingo en el rezo del Ángelus en el Vaticano, donde explicó que, una vez superada la etapa de su operación pulmonar por un tumor canceroso, retomará sus actividades gradualmente. “Una vez superada esta difícil etapa, como saben, retomaré gradualmente mis actividades, siempre con la ayuda de Dios y sus oraciones”, dijo el pontífice, de 71 años, tras el rezo del Ángelus ante los miles de fieles que se congregaron en la plaza de San Pedro. A las doce del mediodía, León XIV apareció en la ventana de sus aposentos en el Palacio Apostólico vaticano, con buen aspecto, sonriente y saludando a los fieles, que le dedicaron una sonora ovación desde la plaza: “Queridos hermanos y hermanas, ¡buen domingo!, fueron sus primeras palabras antes de comenzar con la plegaria del ángelus. Tras el rezo, el pontífice compartió unas reflexiones, en una alocución más breve de lo que suele ser habitual en estos actos y que aprovechó para dar las gracias a todos los que han orado por él en estos días: “He sentido profundamente su apoyo. ¡Muchas gracias!”. También dedicó su especial gratitud a los médicos, enfermeras y todo el personal del Políclinico Gemelli, donde el pasado martes fue operado de un adenocarcinoma en su pulmón derecho y donde ha estado ingresado hasta ayer sábado, recuperándose de la cirugía. “Esta experiencia me ha acercado especialmente a quienes sufren enfermedades y dolencias”, manifestó Robert Prevost, cuya reaparición en el ángelus duró unos ocho minutos, incluyendo plegaria y alocución posterior. En la plaza de San Pedro, los fieles vivieron con emoción y alegría la reaparición del papa este domingo, según testimonios recabados por EFE: “Pensábamos que no lo íbamos a ver, estamos contentas porque la divina providencia lo permitió”, manifestaron Cindy y Emilia, dos colombianas que expresaron su deseo de que el papa mejore “y lo tengamos muchos años más”. “Tenemos fe en que va a salir todo bien”, decían convencidas Patricia y Rose Esperanza, procedentes de California (EE.UU), para quienes ver hoy a León XIV ha sido “un sueño”. También Ernesto Villegas, sacerdote venezolano, reconocía que el de este domingo ha sido un ángelus de mucha expectación y elogió la fortaleza del pontífice: “El papa ha demostrado es un hombre de armas tomar, no se acobarda, retoma su agenda y sigue adelante como buen pastor que sigue dando la vida por sus ovejas”, dijo a EFE. Hace justo una semana que León XIV, en este mismo rezo, anunció por sorpresa a todo el mundo una inminente operación por la detección de un nódulo en un pulmón. La operación se produjo dos días después, el martes por la tarde, en el hospital Gemelli de Roma: el parte médico posterior informó de la extirpación del lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho del papa por un adenocarcinoma, un tipo de cáncer. En los días posteriores, León XIV ha tenido una recuperación favorable y, en el momento de su alta, presentaba unas condiciones clínicas “absolutamente satisfactorias”, según Stefano Margaritora, el cirujano que le operó y que dirige la unidad de Cirugía Torácica del Gemelli. La reaparición del papa en el ángelus desde el Vaticano ha despertado expectación también por la posibilidad de que ofreciera detalles sobre su tratamiento o sobre el viaje a Argentina, Uruguay y Perú que está programado del 6 al 17 de noviembre, si bien Robert Prevost no ha hecho referencia a estos temas. Ayer sábado, en una entrevista a medios vaticanos, su cirujano afirmó que el papa puede afrontar esa visita apostólica: “Diría que no hay motivos clínicos por los que no se pueda realizar ese viaje”, manifestó el doctor Margaritora. En esta primera gira latinoamericana del pontificado de León XIV están previstos hasta 14 vuelos, más de cuarenta discursos y reuniones, nueve misas multitudinarias, así como la visita a Cusco, una ciudad situada a más de 3.000 metros sobre el nivel del mar. articles.title: Embedded AI evaluators won't be an easy solution, Hugging Face's policy chief says | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking — the supposedly neutral and accurate system of evaluations that are designed to measure
articles.body_text: AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking — the supposedly neutral and accurate system of evaluations that are designed to measure whether one AI product is better than another. However, the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, said Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, during a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt last week. Testing needs to come together into a more consistent science if the industry is to rely on them in the future. With that in mind, can we trust the current tests that are being released? “Trust is such a weighted term,” said Solaiman. “In terms of whether we can trust results, one big part [of that] is can you reproduce the results of an evaluation? Do you have the level of access that you need to the model itself — this is where open weights come in in a big way,” she added. Reproducibility in model evaluations has long remained one of the stickier aspects of benchmarking — and remains a topic of significant debate in the industry. Outside of an individual test’s validity, there’s also the added question of how that test compares to other evaluations. “They are an evolving science — where we don’t know how to meaningfully compare them to each other,” Solaiman said. “They start to get ineffective relatively quickly, and we don’t have as much of a thriving ecosystem as we need,” she added. “There’s this hunger for an embedded evaluator ecosystem now, but the qualifications that determine who is an effective evaluator across what tasks need a lot more standardization.” The idea of embedded evaluators — in which supposedly “neutral” third-party observers are placed inside AI organizations — has been popularized over the last several months, as AI labs grapple with a rash of safety incidents that have spurred concerns over the potential harms of their technology. Hugging Face was famously the target of one of those incidents. Instead of active government regulation to identify and mitigate model safety concerns, labs have pushed for the third-party solution. However, doubts remain over how neutral or effective those evaluators will actually be. Anthropic’s decision to hire Accenture as its first evaluator spurred a good amount of backlash, with some critics mocking the idea that the consulting firm was qualified to do the task at hand. Evaluations are now moving from merely a test of the model itself to a test of the entire system around the model — including the harness and agent. The harness — or the tool the user is using to access the model — specifically, has a lot to do with a model’s performance, and a weaker model with a better harness could easily out perform a frontier model, Soleiman shared. “Agentic evals are really hard and really expensive,” said Solaiman. “We have just more evaluations for models. … We don’t have as many evaluations for harnesses, and we are developing better evaluations for the holistic agent — because that’s what a lot of folks are getting value out of,” she added.

articles.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon wants to break Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch, the free toolkit used to build most AI apps, so that more developers run their apps on alternative chips like its own.
articles.body_text: On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at the software advantage that has helped Nvidia become the default hardware choice for AI apps and spurred its rise as AI hardware provider of choice. TorchNeuron works with PyTorch, a free, open source toolkit that developers use to build, train, and run AI models. It lets AI apps written with PyTorch run on Trainium by changing just one line of configuration, according to Amazon — no code rewrite required. Amazon says about 85% of AI apps are written with PyTorch. Facebook originally developed it, but since 2022, it has been part of the Linux Foundation, which maintains open source projects. Nvidia has spent years ensuring its CUDA software — the software infrastructure that allows apps to run on Nvidia GPUs and its other hardware — seamlessly supports AI apps written with PyTorch. As a result, Nvidia’s hardware is now deeply embedded in the toolkit, essentially by default. TorchNeuron is adapted from PyTorch, so developers who know PyTorch already know how to use it. Amazon isn’t the first company to attempt to easily bring their chips to the platform. PyTorch users can also port their apps to AMD GPUs or even Apple’s chips with a simple configuration change. However, Amazon argues that porting to Trainium is not only easy, but it also gives AI startups access to Amazon’s entire cloud. Unsurprisingly, AWS claims that this is a better choice for startups than using neoclouds, many of which are tied to Nvidia and its hardware, like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Firmus. “You’re building on AWS. You’re not betting on a single-purpose compute provider and scrambling to build everything else around it,” Colin Brace, VP of Technology Software at AWS Annapurna Labs (the unit that makes Amazon’s custom chips), told TechCrunch via email. “On AWS,” he continued, “the infrastructure to go from prototype to production is already there, allowing a founder to move fast and scale when they need to.” AWS says that because the same chip both handles training (teaching the AI model) and inference (putting the finished model to work, as when it answers a user’s question), and is tightly integrated with the cloud infrastructure that startups need, its cloud will save them money, even if AWS doesn’t offer the cheapest per-token price. “Trainium’s value is price-performance plus the fact that it’s one platform for both training and inference, which improves the economics across a full workload,” Brace said. “Look at Deepgram — they moved to Trainium using native PyTorch support and they’re processing 70% more audio per dollar at production-grade accuracy.” Deepgram is an AI voice app provider, a competitor to ElevenLabs. But Amazon isn’t content to just give PyTorch app developers an easy option to move to its cloud. Amazon also says it is pushing PyTorch to be less automatically centered on Nvidia, and it will contribute the code to do that to the main PyTorch project. In the blog post announcing the new tool, the company wrote : Amazon’s approach extends beyond its own hardware. The company is contributing changes upstream to PyTorch itself, working with the PyTorch community to remove code that ties the framework to specific chips. The goal is to make PyTorch more hardware-agnostic for the entire developer community, not just Trainium users. While such a tactic is undoubtedly good for those who are selling hardware and cloud services that compete with Nvidia, one of the points of PyTorch is to hide all the pesky difficulties of getting AI code to run on hardware. We’ll have to wait and see if pushing Nvidia out that far gives developers more choice and more affordable options, as Amazon promises, or just more configuration headaches.

articles.title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent that's become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor. But hackers got into part of its online platform and stole some users’ API keys, and the AI tools it turned to for help kept refusing to look at the malicious code.
articles.body_text: OpenCode , an open source AI coding agent that has been gaining ground among developers as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said Saturday that attackers broke into an older system overnight, affecting 1.4% of users of its online platform, OpenCode Console, where some users store the API keys, or digital passwords, they use to access AI services. As the OpenCode team struggled to keep pace with the attack, the scramble to respond highlighted a growing problem: Companies without vetted access to AI models with fewer safety restrictions have a hard time defending against large-scale, AI-driven cyberattacks. “We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the company wrote on X. “We have notified them all this morning via email.” Users who did not receive an email were not impacted, the company said. While the company didn’t specify how the distillation attack occurred, leaked API keys can help users in countries with restricted access to American models generate the high volume of outputs needed for that process. Some skeptics called the framing an overstretch, arguing that the incident was a straightforward breach whose use for distillation remains unproven. Overnight, developers began posting spending alerts and unauthorized charges on Reddit and X: “I saw my Open AI, Anthropic, and Google AI spend alerts all fire off before going to bed wondering what was going on,” a developer wrote . Other users reported charges in the hundreds of dollars on individual accounts; a few described totals above $1,000. Anthropic and Google both blocked the API keys they believed were exposed, while OpenAI said it worked with OpenCode to restore access and refund its API customers for credits used in the attack. OpenCode said refunds for unauthorized charges are underway. The exposed keys were confined to Console, where some users had them in workspaces. The open source app and command-line tool were not affected, according to co-founder Dax Raad. “Note this is the OpenCode Console, not OpenCode itself, those keys never come to us,” he wrote on X. Even as users and AI companies moved to disable the exposed keys, the OpenCode team was still under pressure. Raad said attackers had been trying to break into its systems nonstop for 48 hours, requiring the team to keep AI defensive agents running around the clock. AI models that the OpenCode team turned to for analysis helped for a while, but started refusing to work when the malicious code they were asked to examine activated safety filters. “[T]hat was a bit frustrating,” he wrote on X. OpenCode later received access to OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue program, which gives vetted users AI models that are less likely to refuse requests for defensive security work. Raad said the access improved the team’s ability to investigate the attack. OpenCode isn’t the first company to hit this wall. In July, AI platform Hugging Face said commercial AI models blocked its attempts to analyze activity logs from an intrusion by autonomous AI agents, which OpenAI later revealed were its own models running with safeguards lowered during a test. In a section of its blog post titled “The asymmetry problem,” Hugging Face wrote that guardrails “cannot distinguish an incident responder from an attacker.”

articles.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI companion app Tolan has raised another $30 million after attracting more than 250,000 active users.
articles.body_text: Tolan , the AI companion designed to help people manage their daily lives, navigate relationships and emotions, and accomplish their goals, has just expanded its runway with another $30 million in capital. The startup’s investors in the latest round include Union Square Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Homebrew, doubling the total amount it has raised to date and pushing its valuation beyond the previous $120 million, according to a new report by Upstarts Media . (The startup didn’t disclose its new valuation, but PitchBook estimates it at more than $268 million, with “medium confidence.”) Users engage with Tolan’s app through a cartoonish character that’s meant to offer support and help them get through their to-dos. Tolan generates revenue from its tiered memberships, which are required for full access to all features. The company told Upstarts Media its annual recurring revenue is now in the “double-digit millions.” The startup is one of the few AI companions that have found some traction, as it claims to have more than 250,000 active users who have had more than 70 million conversations over the past year. Around 70% of its users are women, and 40% are parents, Tolan’s team told the news outlet. (Anecdotally, the app is said to appeal in particular to neurodivergent people , who may benefit from additional support, whether that’s emotional support or help with organizing tasks.) Compared with other companions, Tolan seems to have found a balance between being helpful without being perceived as too weird. Compare that with the public shaming that Friend’s pendant-based AI companion faced; users dubbed Friend “ very cringe ,” The New York Times called it “hated,” and Wired said it “has no soul.” Meanwhile, another former top contender in the space, Character.AI, recently filed for bankruptcy after its founder’s return to Google . (Its remaining staff is transitioning to Disney, which bought some of its assets.) However, Tolan could end up facing increased competition from the more recent crop of AI agents, which help users plan, organize, and accomplish their tasks and goals, not just talk their way through them. For instance, Meta gave its AI agent Muse a cute avatar for its users to talk to, which it also plans to release as a hardware product in the future. The startup also has to navigate the risks of offering AI-powered emotional support, given that multiple lawsuits have been filed against general-purpose AI app makers alleging that chatbot interactions contributed to users’ suicides. articles.title: AI assistant startup Town nabs unicorn valuation 4 months after launch | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI assistant startup Town nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures.
articles.body_text: Town, a two-year-old, San Francisco-based startup developing AI assistants, nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B funding round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures. The company launched publicly just four months ago and said it reached millions of dollars in annual recurring revenue in a matter of weeks. It has raised at least $160 million to date, having previously announced a $55 million Series A round in June. Town — founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze — is one of many AI assistants flooding the market right now. Town targets businesses, giving each employee an AI assistant called a Townie that helps with tasks by connecting to tools such as emails and calendars, as well as other core work systems. Employees’ Townies can talk to each other and share approved information; they can also now work with customers and others outside the company. Alongside the funding, Town announced a shared workflow that automatically updates employees’ Townies with new business information rather than requiring each worker to update their own Townie. Andreessen Horowitz, Serena Ventures, and First Round Capital also participated in the round. We’ve reached out to the company for comment. articles.title: Rivian's CEO says autonomy will enable 'dramatically different' vehicle designs | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said he thinks autonomy will allow his company to build radically different kinds of vehicles than the outdoorsy SUVs and trucks it currently makes.
articles.body_text: Rivian is going full steam ahead on developing autonomous vehicle software for its EVs, to the point that it is willing to delay profitability . Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said last week at TechCrunch Disrupt that he thinks autonomy will allow his company to build radically different kinds of vehicles than the outdoorsy SUVs and trucks it currently makes. “Where it gets really interesting is when you think beyond R2 and R3 and start to imagine the form factors that you want to build for a personally owned autonomous vehicle. You know, it opens up all kinds of design opportunities. It can create dramatically different experiences,” he said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I’m wildly excited about what the next 10 years look like in transportation because of what this enables us to dream and think about.” This is not a new idea, to be sure. A decade ago, autonomous vehicle companies, legacy automakers, and many others promised that autonomy, combined with the proliferation of battery-electric drivetrains (which are simpler and take up less space than their gas-powered predecessors), would produce a Cambrian explosion of new mobility form factors. This led to all kinds of crazy concepts getting bandied about at the time. Mercedes-Benz touted a bubbly pod-like design , as well as a long sedan packed with tech . Toyota and others dreamed up “ rooms on wheels .” Hyundai once even showed off its idea for a car with legs . This promised design revolution never escaped the concept and prototyping phase. Autonomy took longer than those companies anticipated to develop, and automakers (new and old) struggled with the harsh realities of manufacturing and selling an entirely new category of vehicle. The difference now is that Scaringe’s comments come at a time when there are real robotaxis roaming the streets of multiple cities around the world. The software that powers them has seemingly developed to a level that is capable enough to operate them safely on public roads at scale, even if there are still some issues to work out when it comes to integrating them into the urban fabric of cars, bikes, pedestrians, and emergency vehicles. The components that make up electric vehicle motors and batteries have gotten cheaper, and companies like Tesla and Rivian (and many more in China) have gotten better at building them at scale. Rivian has a lot of work ahead before it gets to driverless vehicles. The company is at the beginning of its effort to scale production of the R2 SUV, which it needs to get right in order to reverse years of losses that it incurred to become a major EV player. On the autonomy side, Rivian is just a few years removed from completely reworking its approach to self-driving software, and it still has a ways to go. The company has shipped a driver-assistance system that allows drivers to take their hands off the wheel, while still watching the road. It has promised that, by the end of this year, that software will be capable of driving from start to finish — which the company calls “point-to-point navigation” — without intervention, though still under driver supervision. And it is working toward full autonomy, which it plans to deploy in robotaxi versions of its R2 SUV that will be available on Uber’s ride-hail app. But if Rivian achieves full autonomy, most of that driving will be done in personally owned vehicles, Scaringe said in the interview, echoing previous comments he’s made. “You know, 95% of the miles driven in the United States — so this is trillions of miles — 95% of these miles are in things that we personally own, so like you own it, or your household owns it. And so our view is it’s unlikely, even with Level 4 capabilities, that we’re going to see a dramatic societal shift away from that,” he said, referencing the Society of Automotive Engineers’ classification for autonomous vehicles that operate in a specific area. That figure “may go from 95% to 90%, it may go from 95% to 80%, but still the vast majority of the miles driven for a lot of societal and psychological reasons are likely to stay the same,” he said.

articles.title: Amazon to fund 12 small nuclear reactors at former Indiana coal plant | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon and X-energy have inked another deal to deploy nuclear power to the grid. This one will generate nearly 1 gigawatt of electricity.
articles.body_text: Amazon is funding development of a proposed 960-megawatt nuclear plant in Indiana and would be the first customer to buy its power, the companies announced Monday. Utility company American Electric Power (AEP) would operate the plant. X-energy, which designs small modular nuclear reactors and went public in April, would supply the reactors. The new power plant would consist of 12 Xe-100 small modular reactors and be located on the site of a demolished coal power plant just south of Terre Haute. The deal is the second commercial agreement between Amazon and X-energy, and it’s three times larger than the first , which was announced two years ago. Amazon has invested heavily in X-energy, leading a $700 million Series C-1 round in October 2024. The two companies have said they ultimately plan to build 5 gigawatts of new nuclear generating capacity in the U.S. by 2039. Unlike many newly announced power plants, these reactors would be connected to the public electric grid, though Amazon says the power would also serve its data centers. The companies’ aggressive timeline still depends on X-energy successfully delivering its first power plant at a Dow Chemical plant southeast of Houston, Texas. The site, called Seadrift, has recently been at the center of a lawsuit filed by the state of Texas, which accuses the plant of “habitual non-compliance” with water and solid-waste regulations and permits. X-energy has yet to break ground at Seadrift, which will host four Xe-100 reactors to provide the chemical plant with heat and electricity. The company said its construction permit is in the final phases of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s review process. Startups and large cloud computing companies are betting that small modular reactors (SMRs), like the kind being developed by X-energy, will help pull the nuclear industry out of its slump. The most recent nuclear power plants built in the U.S. suffered from egregious budget overruns and slipped timelines. By shrinking the reactor, companies like X-energy hope that mass manufacturing will keep costs and schedules in line. Even then, it could be a tall order. Experts say mass manufacturing often doesn’t start producing benefits for about a decade . X-energy debuted on the Nasdaq in April in an IPO priced at $23 per share. Investor excitement drove the price up 27% in the first day of trading, but shares of the newly public company have dropped by nearly two-thirds since then. News of the Amazon deal sent X-energy’s shares up about 10% in premarket trading, though they were down by less than 2% at the time of publication. articles.title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Fed up with ads, tracking, and sluggish interfaces, some smart TV owners are turning to AI agents to strip away bloatware and take back control of their TVs.
articles.body_text: The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more. One such solution, called “dumbtv,” describes its mission on its GitHub page thus: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.” Another, “ cleanyourtv ,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV. While hacking consumer electronics devices to gain more control over their systems is hardly a new idea, the latest advances in AI technology have made such efforts much more accessible to anyone. With smart TVs in particular, the hacks come at a time when people have grown frustrated with being forced to watch ads and put up with their devices surveilling their viewing habits. Modern smart TVs ship with a technology called automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what’s playing on the screen using screenshots, audio clips, or other forms of digital fingerprinting. If these “dumb TV” hacks become more popular among everyday consumers, they have the potential to disrupt the smart TV ad industry, which profits from selling viewing data to advertisers or using it to display personalized ads on their own interfaces. As the creator of cleanyourtv, Gathin T., puts it, the idea to clean up the smart TV interface started one afternoon when he got tired of seeing the ads on his parents’ TV set. Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon! It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher. Looks like an Apple TV now lol pic.twitter.com/E5Q4A1b0yI “I had Claude Code clean it up over Wi-Fi and build a simple home screen with just their apps on it. I put the prompt on GitHub, tweeted the before and after, and a few thousand people did the same to their own TVs over the next two days. Xiaomi, TCL, Sony, Fire TV, LG, a projector or two,” the developer wrote on a website for donations, linked from the project’s homepage . The solution doesn’t require gaining root access to the TV, nor does it make it impossible to return to the factory default state, if desired. Meanwhile, the dumbtv solution has been tested end-to-end on a Fire TV Edition television set and Android/Google TV platforms on TVs from Sony, TCL, Philips, Hisense, Xiaomi, and Shield. To use this hack, the developer, Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala, suggests pointing your preferred AI agent at the dumbtv repository on GitHub. Sabuwala said he was motivated to work on dumbtv because he was tired of the ads and not being able to delve directly into the content he wanted to watch. His solution was coded using a combination of Deepseek V4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5, he told TechCrunch, and he plans to maintain the GitHub, adding support for more models over time.

articles.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers and also trying to make on-device, private AI agents a thing.
articles.body_text: Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing. The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a large, 120-billion-parameter model geared for agents used by the enterprise. While it uses fewer parameters than the Nemotron 3 Ultra model, Nvidia says it can deliver similar accuracy in instruction-following and tool-use tasks. At the other end of the spectrum, the company also launched two lightweight Bolt models. These are intended to run locally on the new AI PCs (running the Nvidia RTX Spark chip) and workstations running the DGX Spark. Such PCs, aimed at consumers, programmers, and enterprise knowledge workers, are being released right now into the market through partners like Microsoft and Dell. “Any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier without having to choose between capability and deployability,” Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, wrote in the blog post announcing these models. Nvidia claims that the Super VL completes tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI (Opus 5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Luna, Astra) when post-trained on specific agentic tasks. These tasks include document intelligence, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims, and security attack resilience. While such claims are standard whenever a major tech company announces a new model, Nvidia has backed it up with a list of heavy-hitter companies that it says are using Super VL. These include Skydance, EY, Ramp, Crowdstrike, Perplexity, and Salesforce . Of course, these aren’t the first open-weight models that Nvidia has released that compete with the proprietary frontier labs — companies that are both its customers and its investments. The GPU giant has an entire family of Nemotron models that do everything from multimodal artificial intelligence to reasoning, coding, math, and enterprise automation. However, those fast-growing proprietary AI labs are now looking to many other chips and AI system makers beyond Nvidia to power their needs, like AWS’s Trainium and Cerebras, as well as building their own home-grown chips. So Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers. “Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and own what they build,” Briski wrote. So, while Nvidia hopes to create a new market for itself selling PCs powered by its chips by creating machines that run the models and agents locally, PC users “can delegate everyday projects … without sending those workloads to the cloud,” Briski wrote. Of the two Bolt models, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a 74-billion parameter model designed for local agentic tasks. It is intended to balance speed with reasoning to handle multistep reasoning, tool calling, and web browsing. The smallest Bolt E4B is aimed at conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming later this month, Nvidia says.

The moral bankruptcy of Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz
articles.summary: Two of the most famous investors in Silicon Valley endorsed Donald Trump. This is less about tech generally than their investment portfolio, specifically.
articles.body_text: Last week, the founders of venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz declared their allegiance to Donald Trump in their customary fashion: talking about money on a podcast. “Sorry, Mom,” Ben Horowitz says in an episode of The Ben & Marc Show. “I know you’re going to be mad at me for this. But, like, we have to do it.” Marc Andreessen and Horowitz insist they voted for Democrats until now. They are friends with liberals. They claim to be nervous about the social blowback they will receive for this, especially because of the historically progressive nature of the tech industry and the Bay Area. But given the general movement among their class toward Trump, I think those claims about being nervous are overblown, if not performative. There is, for instance, Elon Musk’s pro-Trump super PAC, which has support from Sequoia Capital’s Shaun Maguire and 8VC’s Joe Lonsdale, among other notables. (The Wall Street Journal reported Musk is planning to donate $45 million a month, which Musk has denied.) There’s the $160 million the crypto movement has put forward in support of crypto-friendly candidates. We can’t forget their VC pal David Sacks speaking at the Republican National Convention. And last but not least, there’s Trump’s running mate choice of JD Vance, a former venture capitalist whose firm’s investors included Peter Thiel, Eric Schmidt, and Andreessen himself. This isn’t a movement. It’s a clique. The podcast itself is an extraordinary performance. At one point, Andreessen concedes that their major problems with President Joe Biden — the ones that led them to support Trump — are what most voters would consider “subsidiary” issues. “It doesn’t have anything to do with the big issues that people care about,” he says. If we take this podcast at face value, we are to believe that these subsidiary issues are the only reason they’ve chosen to endorse and donate to Trump. These subsidiary issues take precedence for Andreessen and Horowitz over, say, mass deportations and Project 2025’s attempt to end no-fault divorce. We are looking at a simple trade against personal liberty — abortion, the rights of gay and trans people, and possibly democracy itself — in favor of crypto, AI, and a tax policy they like better. For Horowitz, “probably the most emotional topic” is crypto — a16z started a $4.5 billion crypto fund in 2022, and the pair believe that the Biden administration has been deeply unfair to crypto. In Horowitz’s view, the Biden administration “basically subverted the rule of law to attack the crypto industry.” Certainly much of the crypto industry prefers Trump. But it seems obvious that there has been a lot of intra-agency squabbling as Congress dithered on passing any laws. To place the blame squarely on Biden is bizarre, particularly when we have Trump’s chaotic previous term as guidance. Sure, Trump is no longer saying Bitcoin is “a scam against the dollar,” as he did in 2021; he is scheduled to speak at the Bitcoin conference this year. But his record in office is not exactly pro-crypto. During the Trump administration, financial regulator FinCEN initially asked the public to provide comments on a crypto rule change over a 15-day period that included Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year’s Eve, and New Year’s Day, which effectively shortened the comment window by four working days. There is also the Ripple Labs enforcement case, in which the SEC is seeking a $1.95 billion fine; it, too, dates to the Trump administration. The pair’s complaints about Gary Gensler, the current head of the Securities and Exchange Commission, are striking. They are particularly annoyed that he won’t pay attention to them. “We’re the largest crypto investors or largest blockchain investors in the world, and we’ve requested meetings with him at least a half a dozen times,” Horowitz says. Gensler has not met with them. Neither, they say, has Senator Elizabeth Warren or Biden himself. In fact, Andreessen makes it clear that he expects presidential attention, something he’s been getting since he was 23. Given the number of times Andreessen and Horowitz make references to various meetings with various politicians, it’s easy to get the impression that they are mostly insulted that they are being treated like ordinary constituents. From crypto, we move to AI, which Andreessen and Horowitz don’t think is being regulated correctly either. According to Horowitz, AI is as powerful as, or more powerful than, the internet and the global computer industry from the 1950s on. “This may be the biggest technological boom of all time,” Andreessen says. Andreessen says in his newsletter-cum-manifesto, “The Little Tech Agenda,” that he is worried that AI will face similar scrutiny to crypto. The FTC has issued guidance to the AI industry that indicated it will pursue companies that exaggerate what their AI can do, say they are using AI when they are not, and recklessly put products on the market without properly analyzing the risks. Meanwhile, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has told lenders that they must supply a reason for a credit denial that’s better than just “computer says no” when using AI models. These regulations have little to do with technology and a lot to do with old-fashioned lying. In the podcast, Andreessen and Horowitz single out Biden’s executive order about artificial intelligence. The order requires companies to disclose the presence of very large models, as well as to provide the government information about what the plans are for the model, what cybersecurity measures are taken to protect those models, and the results of red-team testing for sensitive subjects, among other things. This is in keeping with Horowitz’s assertion about the seriousness of the technology. So what’s the problem? The two focus on computing power. The disclosure requirements apply to “any model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 1026 integer or floating-point operations, or using primarily biological sequence data and using a quantity of computing power greater than 1023 integer or floating-point operations.” Andreessen and Horowitz think specifying such a limit is ridiculous. Little tech “will be snuffed out by this kind of regulation,” Horowitz says. It is perhaps worth noting that nothing above the size specified in the executive order — the size Andreessen and Horowitz object to — even exists yet, according to Arati Prabhakar, Biden’s top tech advisor. The fundamental complaint here is that these two believe that the Biden administration’s approach to AI “enshrine[s] the two or three companies that they believe are the only companies that matter as sort of permanent monopolies,” Andreessen says. “And they’re going to just basically destroy the startup ecosystem underneath that.” Andreessen Horowitz is, of course, invested in that ecosystem, having earmarked $2.25 billion for AI applications and infrastructure. The anti-monopoly rhetoric is in keeping with a16z’s latest marketing push. According to Andreessen’s newsletter, startups are threatened by the government, which is “now far more hostile to new startups than it used to be.” Besides his objections to the way the SEC has increased its oversight of crypto, he is also upset that a stepped-up interest in antitrust has made it more difficult for him to exit investments. “Regulatory agencies are punitively blocking startups from being acquired by the same big companies the government is preferencing in so many other ways,” Andreessen writes. After all, the Federal Trade Commission has launched an inquiry into Big Tech’s partnerships and investments with startups — with the goal of seeing if those partnerships squash competition. The irony is so obvious it’s almost embarrassing to point it out. Andreessen says he is upset that Big Tech is too powerful, but he opposes antitrust action because that blocks a route for VCs to exit. Either you’re comfortable with Big Tech getting bigger, in which case acquisitions are fine, or you want little tech to be competitive, which means blocking industry consolidation. Mainly, it seems that Andreessen believes in cashing out. In the podcast, Andreessen and Horowitz pointedly name Google as a threat to startups. “Google, I think we would all agree, is more powerful than probably 95 percent of countries in the world,” Horowitz says at one point. Google, specifically, is a sore spot with the right wing. Vice presidential nominee Vance has already said it should be broken up. Vance believes Google is controlling information and skewing too far left. Of course, Google’s moderation policies don’t just apply to Google News — they also affect YouTube, which hosts a great many right-wing podcasts without issue. It’s unclear how seriously to take Andreessen and Horowitz’s complaints about Big Tech because the complaints don’t quite square with their behavior. For instance, Facebook is similarly powerful and influential, especially in AI. Andreessen sits on its board. A16z is invested in OpenAI, which has a partnership with Microsoft — and both have lobbied strenuously for more regulation around AI. It sure seems like if a16z wants to change things at those big companies, someone could simply pick up the phone. At this point in the podcast, you could squint and say maybe the concern about AI and crypto is really about technology and progress. But from those two topics, we move on to classic rich guy shit of the most tedious kind: tax reform. Andreessen says it was “the final straw for me. This is the thing that tipped me hard.” They are upset about a proposal to alter capital gains taxes. Capital gains are paid on investment assets, and they are typically paid when the investment is sold and the gains are, in industry terms, “realized.” The new Biden treasury proposal means that for people whose wealth is worth more than $100 million, any unrealized capital gains will be taxed, too. This is what has Andreessen and Horowitz in a tizzy. It means that if they own a clutch of highly valued startup shares, they will have to pay taxes on them before they cash out. This is a “very scary proposal,” Horowitz says. Startups are illiquid assets, Andreessen points out. “Startups never go up and down. They’re never overvalued,” says Horowtiz, dryly. “There’s no bubbles.” Andreessen notes that the way the value of a startup is calculated for the purposes of this proposed tax has to do with the latest round’s valuation. Historically, one of the ways that Andreessen Horowitz has approached startup investing is to inflate a company’s valuation; it is “the OG when it comes to doling out speculative startup valuations.” The new proposed tax punishes this kind of behavior — a high valuation means a high tax. “This makes startups completely implausible,” says Andreessen. “Venture capital just ends. Firms like ours don’t exist.” This is followed by an anxiety spiral that is sort of difficult to convey in text; I suggest you listen for yourself. “California is done,” says Andreessen. “It’s total destruction.” The taxes won’t just target the wealthy; they’ll come for everyone. “Once the structure gets established, the politicians do what they do: they’ll walk the numbers up,” Andreessen says. “Presto chango, we’re Argentina!” says Horowitz. Finally, Horowitz gets ahold of himself. “By the way, this one probably won’t get all the way through the system,” he says. “But it might!” There is another issue that might cause wreckage throughout Silicon Valley. It is immigration. An awful lot of immigrants comprise Silicon Valley’s talent pool — a huge swath of engineers in the US are on H-1B visas. The Trump / Vance ticket is virulently anti-immigrant. The current CEOs of Google, Microsoft, Adobe, and IBM are all immigrants. So are Peter Thiel and Elon Musk. Mark Zuckerberg and Bill Gates are involved in Fwd.us, a lobbying group dedicated to immigration reform that Musk and Sacks both left. If there were an issue that would rally the people who care most about progress, innovation, and talent, you’d think protecting the immigrants who’ve built lives and careers in tech would be it. Stopping immigration is a core issue of the Trump campaign. During the Republican National Convention, delegates held up signs saying “Mass Deportation Now.” Trump has called the H-1B, the visa many tech workers use to come to Silicon Valley, “very bad” and “unfair” to US workers. In his previous term, he targeted H-1B visa applications specifically; in the fiscal year 2018, almost 25 percent of applications were denied, up from about 13 percent the year before. In fiscal year 2019, 20 percent of H-1B applications were denied. The denials plummeted after several Trump administration rules were thrown out by courts; the denial rate in 2022 was just 2 percent. Immigration plainly matters for crypto — as Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin says, “The crypto industry is uniquely international, and so immigration law is crypto law.” Buterin is one of the most influential voices in crypto, and Ethereum is the foundation for a swath of Andreessen Horowitz’s investment portfolio. Among the investments that rely on it are MakerDAO, VeeFriends, Dapper Labs, and EigenLayer. It is remarkable that the founder of Ethereum is saying that voting for Trump is against the crypto ethos, and the big crypto investors are doing it anyway. The word “immigration” is only mentioned by Andreessen and Horowitz in the podcast when they discuss the rally in which someone attempted an assassination: Trump had turned his head to look at a chart that purported to show illegal immigration into the US as the bullet whizzed by. I wondered why such an important issue for tech wasn’t addressed, so I emailed Margit Wennmachers, a16z’s PR guru, to ask. She didn’t reply. After I finished listening to the podcast, a few things kept nagging at me. Take the very beginning of the podcast. Once upon a time, Andreessen says, you could get very rich and then give the money away in philanthropy, “and you get enormous credit for that. And, you know, it absolves you of whatever.” At some point in the last 10 years, some people suggested that maybe rich people should pay more taxes instead of giving their money away — that perhaps the whims of some random rich person are not the best way to support the most vulnerable in our society. Andreessen and Horowitz suggest that this critique of philanthropy is simply jealousy. It also unbalanced “the deal.” “The deal,” as described on the podcast, is vague. To my ear, it sounds like this: Tech companies could basically do whatever they wanted, as long as people who worked there paid high taxes and donated enough money to charitable causes. The money — taxes, donations — made them the good guys. Andreessen and Horowitz point to the mid-2010s — that is, the era of low interest rates — as the time of “the deal” unraveling. Notably, this is around the time that the tech hype cycle became obvious even to people who weren’t paying attention. This year, it’s scooters! Now it’s viral media companies! Now it’s metaverse! Now it’s crypto! Now it’s AI! These ideas were more or less rejected by the market, except possibly AI. The one thing all these hype cycles had in common was VCs talking their books, as publicly as possible. That charge was led by Andreessen Horowitz. So now, instead of investing in things the market wants, Andreessen and Horowitz appear to be gambling on legislation instead. Their timing is remarkable; not even a week after their Trump endorsement, Biden dropped out of the race, rallying the Democrats behind Vice President Kamala Harris. In the hours immediately following the announcement, small-money donors raised $46.7 million for her campaign. By endorsing Trump, Andreessen and Horowitz have effectively lost whatever leverage they might have had with the Harris campaign. But maybe that doesn’t matter. Near the end of the podcast, Horowitz says that he was shaken by the assassination attempt on Donald Trump because he’s friends with Ivanka, his daughter, and Jared Kushner, his son-in-law. “Ivanka and the kids were just at my house,” Horowitz says, of learning Trump was shot. “We went to see David Copperfield and all that. So my brain was almost frozen because I had this feeling about, ‘Oh my god, Grandpa just got shot.’” As for Andreessen, he has been inveighing against “woke” capital, engaging in Twitter culture wars, and complaining about what he views as the media’s hostility to free speech for a while now. In Andreessen’s 2023 “Techno-Optimist Manifesto,” he lists what he terms “patron saints” of the movement. They include Filippo Tommaso Marinetti, an Italian futurist who was also the co-author of The Fascist Manifesto; Nick Land, whose writing is a foundational text for the so-called alt-right; Neven Sesardic, a philosopher who argues that race is biologically real and not socially constructed; and Vilfredo Pareto, who argued that democracy is an illusion. And this talk about democracy brings me to Curtis Yarvin, personal friend of vice presidential candidate Vance. Yarvin, a software developer, is openly anti-democracy. (Yarvin’s recent newsletter, in response to Biden dropping out, enthusiastically advocates for a return to monarchy. Freak shit.) One of Yarvin’s ideas, called “retire all government employees” or RAGE, is part of Project 2025, a Heritage Foundation proposal for what Trump should do if he wins. This rhetoric was echoed by Vance in 2021, who called out Yarvin by name. So this VC cabal is trading against the basic principles of America — not merely against personal freedom, but democracy itself — in the hopes of profit. It’s not the first time tech has made the trade against freedom; IBM made it during the Holocaust. In venture capital, you are what you fund. Andreessen and Horowitz understand this, even embody it. But they aren’t just funding the issues they discuss on their podcast; they are funding Trump and Vance. That means those donations are anti-abortion, anti-immigration, and possibly even anti-democracy because that is what the Trump / Vance ticket stands for. These are not subsidiary issues: these are now what two of Silicon Valley’s most prominent figures now stand for, too. Is that a good investment? Correction July 24: An earlier version of this article misstated the donation strategy of a crypto super PAC. The group also spends money on Democratic candidates, not just right-wing ones.

articles.title: How Big Tech is swallowing the AI industry
articles.summary: Amazon has replicated an antitrust-avoidance playbook pioneered by Microsoft with its hiring of most of the team behind buzzy AI startup Adept.
articles.body_text: A couple of months ago, I was sitting in the audience at a tech conference in San Fransisco watching Bloomberg’s Emily Chang interview Reid Hoffman. She asked about Microsoft’s hiring of the team behind Inflection, a would-be OpenAI competitor that Hoffman co-founded. It was an acquisition in everything but name, clearly designed to avoid the scrutiny of antitrust regulators. Not only had Microsoft (where Hoffman is a board member) hired most of Inflection’s employees — it also licensed the startup’s technology in a way that seemed designed to make its investors whole. Speaking with Chang that day onstage, Hoffman predicted that what happened to Inflection will become a “pattern” for future AI deals. We are seeing that pattern play out now. Last Friday, Amazon announced that it is hiring most of the team behind Adept, another would-be OpenAI competitor that raised about $400 million from top-tier investors to build, in the words of CEO David Luan, “a new type of giant model that turns natural language into actions on your machine.” Alexandra Miller, an Amazon spokesperson, told The Verge that the company had hired “close to” to 66 percent of Adept’s employees. In an internal memo published by GeekWire’s Taylor Soper, SVP Rohit Prasad said that, like Microsoft with Inflection, Amazon will also be licensing Adept’s technology to “accelerate our roadmap for building digital agents that can automate software workflows.” Adept’s corporate blog post about the news suggests it was running out of money: “Continuing with Adept’s initial plan of building both useful general intelligence and an enterprise agent product would’ve required spending significant attention on fundraising for our foundation models, rather than bringing to life our agent vision.” Recent reports say the company has been looking to sell itself. The reality is that building leading AI models is extremely costly, and raising $400 million isn’t even enough to compete these days. Big Tech, meanwhile, is flush with cash and looking to get in on what everyone perceives to be the next big thing. It’s logical for more AI startups to go the way of Inflection and Adept as the industry consolidates. The problem for Big Tech is that they are no longer allowed to buy companies like they once did. The current antitrust enforcement regime would most certainly try to block an Amazon acquisition of Adept, whether there is a strong legal argument for doing so or not. (Amazon execs are still seething about not being allowed to buy a robot vacuum cleaner company.) Even still, capitalism finds a way. What Microsoft did to Inflection, and what Amazon just did to Adept, is the new Big Tech playbook for swallowing the AI industry and getting away with it. Silicon Valley has a storied history of acquihires, where a startup is gutted for its people and left for dead. Microsoft and Amazon have done what are essentially reverse acquihires, where the hiring of people and a corresponding licensing deal is designed to disguise what is actually an acquisition. Reid Hoffman, meanwhile, should probably be congratulated for more than just an accurate prediction about the future of these deals — one of Adept’s earliest investors was none other than his venture capital firm, Greylock. Correction, July 1st: A previous version of this story incorrectly stated the percentage of Adept employees hired by Amazon. The percentage is “close to” 66 percent, not 80 percent.

articles.title: Nordkoreas hot: ”Korsat röda linjen”
articles.summary: Kim Jong-Un riktar nya hot mot Sydkorea. ”De har korsat den röda linjen”, säger diktatorns syster Kim Yo-Jong.
articles.body_text: Kim Jong-Un riktar nya hot mot Sydkorea, skriver New York Post . Nordkorea skyller detta på grannlandets ”vårdslösa beteende”. – De har korsat den röda linjen, säger diktatorns syster Kim Yo-Jong. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Under senare år har spänningarna längs den koreanska gränsen ökat i takt med att Nordkorea har lagt till minor, taggtrådsstängsel och pansarvärnsbarriärer. Tonläget mellan Nordkorea och Sydkorea har intensifierats efter förra månadens minexplosioner som skadade tre sydkoreanska soldater. För två veckor sedan slog Sydkorea fast att grannlandets minor orsakade explosionerna vid gränsen mellan länderna den 21 september. Man uppmanade Nordkorea att be om ursäkt och ta bort andra minor. Nordkorea förnekade att de bar ansvaret för explosionerna och varnade för kraftiga vedergällningar om man provocerades. På måndagen anklagade Kim Yo-Jong, den mäktiga systern till Nordkoreas ledare Kim Jong-Un, Sydkorea för att ha avlossat varningsskott och utfärdat varningssändningar ett flertal gånger vid gränsen sedan augusti. Hon hävdade att grannlandets provokationer ”har korsat den röda linjen” sedan minexplosionerna. – En allvarlig situation råder längs den södra gränsen på grund av de sydkoreanska militära gangstrarnas vårdslösa beteende, säger Kim Yo-Jong. Den nordkoreanska militären överväger nu att ”placera ut fler vapen längs den södra gränsen som en förebyggande åtgärd”, enligt Kim Yo-Jong. Man överväger också att återuppta propagandasändningar mot grannlandet. Sydkoreas militär uppgav tidigare att varningsskotten och varningssändningarna berodde på att nordkoreanska soldater ett 50-tal gånger gjort illegala gränsöverträdelser i år.

articles.title: Pappans desperata jakt efter Carolin
articles.summary: 25-åriga Carolin Schmidt försvann i bergen. Nu söker hennes pappa själv efter dottern i området.
articles.body_text: 25-åriga Carolin Schmidt försvann i bergen. Nu söker hennes pappa själv efter dottern i området. – Man vet aldrig hur någon annan egentligen känner sig, säger fjällstugechefen Andreas Rauth, som träffade mannen under sökandet, till österrikiska Kronen Zeitung . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. 25-åriga tyskan Carolin Schmidt älskar att vandra i bergsområden. Hon sågs senast i Garmisch-Partenkirchen och senaste gången familjen hade kontakt med henne var den 6 september. Sedan dess är Carolin försvunnen. Innan hon försvann tros hon ha vandrat i gränsområdet mellan Österrike och Tyskland . En stor polisinsats med bland annat helikopter för att försöka finna Carolin har hittills varit förgäves. I sex veckor har hennes familj ”desperat väntat på livstecken”, skriver tyska RTL . Nu har hennes pappa tagit saken i egna händer. Nyligen dök en vandrare dök upp vid en fjällstuga vid berget Hohe Munde. – Han presenterade sig som den försvunna unga kvinnans pappa, säger stugans chef Andreas Rauth. Mannen bad att få sätta upp en lapp i stugan angående sin försvunna dotter. – Det var förstås en självklarhet att göra honom den tjänsten, säger Rauth. Mannen berättade att han letade efter Carolin på berg i området och att han tänkte bege sig uppför 2 662 meter höga Hohe Münde under dagen. Rauth avrådde honom från detta.

articles.title: Trumps ord: Putin gör inte ens något
articles.summary: På måndagen pratar Trump om Ukraina. – Ärligt talat har Ryssland överlag betett sig ganska rimligt mot Ukraina. De har inte gjort något särskilt anmärkningsvärt, säger han. Bara i september dödade Ryssland 328 civila ukrainare i drönar- och robotattacker.
articles.body_text: – Ärligt talat har Ryssland överlag betett sig ganska rimligt mot Ukraina. De har inte gjort något särskilt anmärkningsvärt, säger han. Bara i september dödade Ryssland 328 civila ukrainare i drönar- och robotattacker. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Relationen mellan Volodymyr Zelenskyj och Donald Trump är frostigare än på många månader. Anledningen är Trumps beslut att börja köpa rysk diesel från Putin. Ordkriget mellan de båda har fortsatt i veckan, då Zelenskyj menade att Trump ”står på fel sida av historien”. – Han vet inte vad han pratar om. Jag tror inte ens han vill avsluta kriget, säger Trump på måndagen. – Ärligt talat har Ryssland överlag betett sig ganska rimligt gentemot Ukraina. De har inte gjort något särskilt anmärkningsvärt. På måndagen attackerade ryska drönare en park i staden Nova Vodolaha. Tre kvinnor och två spädbarn dödades. 14 människor skadade också i attacken, rapporterar Kyiv Independent. Attacken ägde rum mitt på dagen när flera familjer hade samlats i parken. Bara i år har ryska drönar- och robotattacker dödat 2 570 civila, och över 15 000 har skadats, enligt statistik från FN. I torsdags förra veckan dödades 33 människor när Ryssland attackerade två linjebussar i Kramatorsk. I helgen attackerade Ryssland även Kievs energiindustri, något som lämnade över 600 000 invånare utan ström.

articles.title: Saba, 24, sköts ihjäl i idrottshall
articles.summary: Saba Abraham, 24, var i idrottshallen för att skapa en trygg mötesplats för barn och unga. Då blev hon ihjälskjuten. – Det är fruktansvärt, att en ung kvinna mister livet på det här sättet, säger stadsdelsdirektör Lee Orberson.
articles.body_text: Saba Abraham, 24, var i idrottshallen för att skapa en trygg mötesplats för barn och unga. – Det är fruktansvärt, att en ung kvinna mister livet på det här sättet, säger stadsdelsdirektör Lee Orberson. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Saba Abraham var anställd av Stockholms stad , på fritidsgården i Älvsjö. Hon arbetade bland annat med Samhällsmatchen, som är samlingsnamnet på Hammarby fotbolls olika insatser i samhället. En sådan insats är spontanfotboll, som anordnas på olika platser i södra Stockholm för att skapa trygga, inkluderande och levande mötesplatser. Vid 21-tiden i fredags kväll var hon ledare vid en sådan spontanfotbollsmatch i Kämpetorpshallarna i Älvsjö när hon blev skjuten. Dagen därpå meddelade polisen att hon var död. – Det är fruktansvärt, att en ung kvinna mister livet på det här sättet. Dessutom är det en av våra medarbetare som jobbar just med att göra det bättre för barn och unga i stadsdelen, säger Lee Orberson, stadsdelsdirektör i Hägersten-Älvsjö. Han beskriver Saba Abraham som en mycket uppskattad medarbetare. – Hon har haft jättestor inverkan på många barn och unga och har gjort ett verkligt gott arbete i att skapa goda förutsättningar för dem. Två tonårspojkar är anhållna på den högre misstankegraden för mordet på Saba. Åklagaren har sagt att han har gott hopp om att mordet kommer att klaras upp. När Expressen besökte minnesplatsen på söndagen var det många som tagit sig dit för att hedra Saba med blommor och ljus. En av dem var en 12-årig flicka, som bland annat brukade träffa kvinnan på ungdomsgården. – Hon var en person som verkligen var där när man kanske har det svårt eller om man bara vill prata med någon. Då kunde man prata med henne utan att hon dömer, sa flickan.

articles.title: Sammanvuxna tvillingar – en fick hjärtstillestånd
articles.summary: 27-åringarna José Luis och José Armando Cevallos var sammanvuxna tvillingar. Sedan fick en av dem hjärtstillestånd.
articles.body_text: 27-åringarna José Luis och José Armando Cevallos var sammanvuxna tvillingar. När läkarna lyckades stabilisera hans tillstånd fick den andre tvillingen en hjärtinfarkt, skriver TMZ Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I tvillingarnas sista inlägg på Instagram för några dagar sedan skrev de: Deras nära vän Fernando Carrillo berättade för tidningen Y Ahora Sonsoles att José Luis förra veckan drabbades av hjärtstillestånd, vilket ledde till att tvillingarna hamnade på sjukhus. articles.title: Därför sonderar C-ledaren: ”Vill visa sina väljare”
articles.summary: Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist (C) vet redan att det inte blir någon mittenregering, enligt statsvetare. Poängen med att sondera är att kunna visa väljare och medlemmar att man verkligen har försökt – innan man väljer sida. – Svängrummet ökar, säger Andreas Johansson Heinö.
articles.body_text: Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist (C) vet redan att det inte blir någon mittenregering, enligt statsvetare. Poängen med att sondera är att kunna visa väljare och medlemmar att man verkligen har försökt – innan man väljer sida. – Svängrummet ökar, säger Andreas Johansson Heinö. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Centerpartiet har före och efter valet sagt att man vill se en mittenregering. På måndagen fick partiledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist sonderingsuppdraget av talmannen för att undersöka möjligheterna att bilda en sådan. Hon har bjudit in alla partiledare till samtal – och samtliga har tackat ja. Andreas Johansson Heinö, statsvetare och förläggare på Timbro, och Johan Hellström, statsvetare vid Umeå universitet, är tämligen säkra på att C-ledarens sondering kommer att misslyckas. De menar i stället att syftet med att ta sig an uppdraget nog är ett annat. – Det finns inget realistiskt mittenalternativ. Partiledarna på den borgerliga sidan har varit tydliga med att de inte har något intresse av att se en regering med Socialdemokraterna, säger Johan Hellström och fortsätter: – Jag tror att Centerpartiet ändå är ganska pigga på att göra det här försöket för att sedan kunna visa för sina egna väljare, förtroendevalda och partiaktiva att de har tömt ut alternativet med en mittenregering innan de börjar samarbeta med Socialdemokraterna. Johan Hellström menar att Centerpartiet egentligen redan har valt sida i politiken: den rödgröna. – Jag har svårt att se att de kan backa från det. Det skulle kosta dem enormt mycket i ett extra val eller i ett kommande ordinarie riksdagsval, säger han.

articles.title: Läraren Alexanders galna fynd på lunchen
articles.summary: Han undervisar om vikingatiden. På lunchpromenaden gjorde SO-läraren Alexander Stoltzberg ett vikingafynd. – Jag försöker göra mina lektioner levande, och detta hjälpte ju till, säger han och skrattar.
articles.body_text: På lunchpromenaden gjorde SO-läraren Alexander Stoltzberg ett vikingafynd. – Jag försöker göra mina lektioner levande, och detta hjälpte ju till, säger han och skrattar. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Något stack upp i marken mitt på stigen. Alexander Stoltzberg lutade sig ner och grävde fram det. Nej, Alexander, som vanligtvis undervisar om vikingatiden, hade gjort ett fynd från just vikingatiden. – Det är på riktigt, på riktigt otroligt, säger han. Alexander arbetar som SO-lärare på en skola i Kungsängen utanför Stockholm, och det var på jobbet under en lunchpromenad som fyndet gjordes, något även Mitt i rapporterat om. När han kom hem tittade han närmare på föremålet, och förstod att det var gammalt. Ett par dagar senare lämnade han in det till Riksantikvarieämbetet i Stockholm som bekräftade: det är en vikingatida remdelare av brons, en del av en hästutrustning från perioden 800–1050. Enligt Alexander har liknande fynd gjort i Storbritannien och kopplas till tidigt 1000-tal. – När beskedet kom skrattade jag och mina elever tillsammans. Jag försöker göra mina lektioner levande, och detta hjälpte ju till, säger han och skrattar. Fyndet beskrivs som ”ytterst ovanligt” i Skandinavien. ”Eftersom området där fyndet påträffades är hårt exploaterat utan kända fornlämningar är det svårt att veta varifrån och från vilken kontext föremålet ursprungligen kommer”, skriver Riksantikvarieämbetet i sitt beslut.
